text:
eve: quick flag: kernel-selector rollout is causing unexpected host overhead in prod-shadow tests. p50 +5ms on 50-150 token requests.
noah: saw that too. any perf traces? is this parse or network syscall noise?
rachel: dumping a small flamegraph from a repro: \n```\nhost_accept -> parse_request -> preparse_split -> compress_fragments -> writev\n- parse_request: 3.8ms (was 1.0ms)\n- writev calls per req: 3 (was 1)\n```\nlots of extra tiny frames.
perf-bot: perf-sample: host_parse.cpu_cycles +38%, syscalls.writev +2.7x for affected requests.
eve: interestingly kvcache.hit_rate dips at the same time. looks like prefix coalescing broken by earlier split.noah: hypothesis: kernel selector changed windowing so preparse decides to flush prefix earlier. that splits what used to be one request prefix into two frames -> kvcache misses + more syscalls.
rachel: tried a local config tweak: set preparse.coalesce_threshold=192 and kernel_selector.max_miniwindow=64 for seq < 200. quick numbers: parse back to 1.2ms, writev calls down to 1.1, kvcache hit +4.1%.
deploy-bot: applying canary config to canary-2: roll id c-2026-0501-7.
perf-bot: canary sampling (n=2800): host p50 improved -4.7ms, p95 -9.8ms; kvcache.hit_rate delta +3.9%.
eve: plan: keep kernel change, but gate preparse.coalesce for small buckets (<=200). add perf-suite microtest for micro-host-path <256 tokens and a kvcache delta alert at 3%. also add a short changelog blurb about kernel selector windowing so SRE isn't surprised.
noah: i'll author the perf test PR and the rollback playbook. rachel: can you add an integration test to prevent accidental preparse.coalesce flips?
rachel: on it. adding the flamegraphs, perf counters and config diffs to the ticket.
eve: thanks. monitor canary for 1h, if stable roll to prod. :white_check_mark:
